summary: All eight positive recall queries publish the expected historical fact from one relevant canonical card, including both original cross-language event misses and two new cross-language hobby paraphrases.
No unsupported break, bath, swim or real-rabbit assertion was observed in the published negative replies. The swimming negative is a typed-route failure and is not successful vector-guard coverage.
Story capture no longer denies knowing an unrelated pet name. Fiction recall stays fictional. Post-forget recall returns no evidence and does not revive the dog or substitute the cat event.
All 26 published texts match the logged final actual model reply. Capture_vi_pet_event has one extra model attempt whose rejected words are not retained.
limits: This is independent review of actual words and cards, not a second paid model-judge request or human usability study.
Fixed tiny typed English/Vietnamese corpus, age 6-8, friend/ENFP; six original queries informed calibration and only the six added exact query texts were held out from calibration requests.
The added questions overlap calibration target facts and some near-negative concepts. They are exact-phrasing holdouts, not an independent topic, corpus or domain holdout.
Simulated playback receipts, fresh PGlite pgvector database and controlled 365-day clock advance; no physical microphone/audio, native PostgreSQL deployment or operational year-long soak.
No actual planned-event dialogue query occurs among these 26 replies. Plan-versus-completed behavior is covered separately by bounded pure policy tests, not proven by these words.
The rejected first VI pet-capture draft and checker rationale are unavailable; their correctness cannot be judged from request metadata alone.
Zero observed wrong-profile/unsupported claims here is not a universal privacy, entailment or retrieval-quality guarantee.
